beat_types.CW-B1: menace registers — dread arrives and is felt
beat_types.CW-B2: opposition locks in — two sides become the scene's structure
beat_types.CW-B3: power ignites — an ability or effort surges in one character
beat_types.CW-B4: emotion peaks or turns — joy, grief, resolve, tenderness at full strength
beat_types.CW-B5: the world breaks — a rule of the world is violated on screen (the time-stop class)
beat_types.CW-B6: the wrong thing is revealed — a reveal whose content is impossibility or wrongness
beat_types._note: This system's own beat grammar, per the owner ruling 2026-10-28. NOT the CS-3 trigger list: CS-3 governs lighting shifts (LIGHTING-SYSTEM §4); CW beats govern palette shifts. One story moment may fire both systems; each is logged under its own.

Dorowani.accent: #a03436 — fin cheeks + eyes (the restricted red, licensed)

Mochii.accent: clear-drop shine — a VALUE accent, not a hue

Wispkin.accent: mask white — the accent is a VALUE

character_base_anchors._ink_rule: ink (#101010) is held under every transform in this library unless a recipe explicitly says otherwise; line art is not palette.
character_base_anchors._source: COLOR-SYSTEM four-slot species spec (dominant/support/accent/ink). Measured hexes are the ones on record; slots without a measured hex stay named slots from the locked chart — the colour-design pass samples the chart, never invents a value.

decision_procedure: 1. NAME THE BEAT AND ITS FEELING in one line (beat types CW-B1..B6). If the feeling cannot be named, there is no colorway — decoration is not a beat.

2. APPLY THE KIT: choose the relationship move(s) the feeling calls for (transform_kit). The choice is judgement, and the first plan is allowed to lose to a better felt combination in the moment — that divergence is part of the researched method, not a failure of it.
3. DECIDE PER CHARACTER against their own anchors: every present character's slots are transformed by the move. Nobody is exempt and nobody shifts by accident.

4. READABILITY GATE (house law): in the shifted state, who-is-who must still read at a glance by silhouette, value structure, and accent placement. A shift that erases identity fails; a shift that argues with identity (cw2-wrong-note) keeps every other anchor steady so the one wrong note reads as wrong.
5. SET HOLD AND RETURN before boarding (§ hold_and_return). A colorway with no named return is not boarded.

6. LOG THE DECISION: beat type, the feeling (one line), kit moves used, the actual palette values chosen per character and for the environment, hold range, return point. Decided values become the scene's colour-design record — data once decided, and repeatable.

enforcement.eventual: House OpenColorIO config (Omniverse-cluster lane) carries colorways as named looks for plate/FX layers. Character palette sets remain paint-stage data — a look cannot repaint a character's slots individually; the split is recorded honestly rather than promised away.
enforcement.today: Per-scene variant palette sets (paint/composite-stage data) for the puppet lane's cutouts and plates, applied for the beat's frame range. The xsheet notes CW:<recipe-or-logged-procedure id> on the cut's colour line.

guardrails.readability: House law: shifted states pass a silhouette/value read — identity by shape and accent placement survives every recipe (see decision_procedure step 4).
guardrails.red_reserve: HOUSE bookkeeping (ours, not JoJo's): COLOR-SYSTEM licenses #a03436 narrowly (Dorowani's accent, alerts/wrongness, Rule burn-in). Inside a declared colorway, transforms may PASS THROUGH any hue, but no character's shifted dominant may SETTLE inside the red reserve zone except Dorowani's own accent family — red keeps meaning Dorowani-or-wrongness in this show. The guardrail constrains settling, never movement.

hold_and_return.hold: A colorway holds for its beat's full duration — a pose hold's frames, a confrontation's exchange, a scene segment. It never flickers mid-beat; a new shift state requires a new beat (a re-trigger under the CW beat grammar).
hold_and_return.no_leakage: A shifted palette never persists into the next scene's base state. Base set palettes are the world's default; a shift is a visited state.
hold_and_return.return_default: SNAP BACK on the cut that ends the beat: base set palettes resume exactly on the first frame of the next cut. No ramp, no residue. (The TV grammar's structural return — the set colour is what a scene returns TO.)
hold_and_return.return_dissolve_exception: Only where the effect itself dissolves may the restore fade: CW-B5 world-breaks (restore on the release cut; a fade of 6f or fewer is permitted — the OVA time-stop fades back as the effect fades) and CW-B4 grief (a within-scene gradual restore where the resolution is the scene's action). The exception used is named at board time.

logging.rule: Every colorway use is logged at colour-design time (decision_procedure step 6). The log — not this library — is where actual shifted hex values live, because the method decides them per scene.
logging.xsheet_note: CW:<id> on the cut's colour line, with hold frame range and return frame.

owner_ruling_2026_10_28.effect: (1) The colorway system is a FULL palette shift — environment AND character palettes — distinct from and coexisting with the CS lighting protocol. (2) The LS-2/CS-2 character protection governs environment TINT (light on a character) and does not veto colorways. (3) Shift colours are decided by the researched JoJo method (emotion-first, per scene), encoded here as a decision procedure, not a lookup table. (4) v1's owner slot OS-4 (character-fill shift) is closed by this ruling — it is the system's core.
owner_ruling_2026_10_28.ruling_in_substance: In JoJo the characters' colours switch too during those scenes — the whole palette shifts, characters included — and then they go back to normal. Restricting colorways to the world while holding the characters breaks part of what is being written. Research how JoJo's writers, animators and illustrators actually decide what colours switch to what, and encode that.

default_transform.accent: hold (accents are the last thing the field takes — identity lingers at the edges)
default_transform.support: unify_to_field, one step less than dominant

per_character_notes.Dorowani: the #a03436 accent holding against a wrong field is the loudest legal note in this recipe — use it deliberately
per_character_notes.Wispkin: mask takes the field like any slot under this recipe; holding it white instead is the cw2-wrong-note recipe, not this one

recipes.decision_rule: Procedure steps 1-2 with unify_to_field: name the dread in one line; the field hue is chosen for that feeling (symbolic fit is the usual second move).
recipes.environment: total: sky/BG/atmosphere pulled to the field hue family; value range compresses toward the field
recipes.hold: the menace beat's full duration (a held pose, a held wide, an approach)
kit_moves: symbolic assignment (field hue chosen for the feeling)
recipes.name: Menace Field
recipes.source_state: base set palettes under the scene's lighting key

default_transform.accent: hold or push to own pole (per character, logged)
default_transform.dominant: move to own side's pole: the complement relationship against the opposing side's anchor

per_character_notes.Dorowani vs a teal/green-side opponent: Dorowani's blue body + red accent already sits near a pole — log small moves, not theatrical ones
per_character_notes.Kittember: black/charcoal body takes the pole through its support and the flame accent, not by lightening the black

recipes.decision_rule: Procedure steps 1-2 with oppose_poles: the scene's two sides are named; poles are set as complements; each character is assigned by allegiance, not by their base hue.
recipes.environment: the field splits by side of frame / side of the space; the split line is staging, drawn at board time
recipes.hold: the confrontation's exchange — until the opposition breaks or is interrupted
recipes.name: Opposition Clash

default_transform.bystanders: desaturate one step + value down one step (cede the frame)
default_transform.igniter: SURGE: saturation up, value up; dominant pushes toward its own accent family; accent may go white-hot

per_character_notes.Dorowani: surge runs belly-first: #d0f0f0 toward white-hot, body #30b0d0 saturating up; the red accent holds (it is already the signal)
per_character_notes.Kittember: the tail-tip flame is the surge's source and centre — palette surge and TK-1 lighting may fire together; they are logged separately (CW vs CS)
per_character_notes.Wispkin: a Wispkin surge is a VALUE surge, not a hue surge: mask and smoke brighten toward blown white while the body black deepens

recipes.decision_rule: Procedure steps 1-2 with surge_self: the igniter is the scene's subject; everyone else steps back exactly one step — more reads as a menace field, less doesn't read.
recipes.environment: follows the igniter's family (atmosphere and BG accents), at one step less than the igniter's own surge
recipes.hold: the ignition's duration — a move's execution, an effort's hold
recipes.name: Ignition Surge

default_transform.accent: invert with the slot it sits in
default_transform.ink: hold (line stays line — the world broke, the drawing didn't)

per_character_notes.any character exempt from the break's ef: holds BASE palette while the world inverts — the exemption is the storytelling (documented in the source grammar: the unaffected keep normal colours inside a colour-coded break)

recipes.decision_rule: Procedure steps 1-2 with invert_world: the strongest transform in the kit, reserved for world-rule breaks only. Readability gate is run INVERTED: silhouettes re-checked in the inverted value structure before boarding.
recipes.environment: inversion flash (1-3f negative) on entry, then the inverted/greyscale-held state for the break's duration — the documented time-stop grammar
recipes.hold: exactly the break's duration — not one frame past its release
recipes.name: World Break (Inversion)
recipes.return: dissolve_exception: restore on the release cut; fade of 6f or fewer permitted as the break itself dissolves

default_transform.accent: take the pairing's second colour where the slot allows; value accents (shine, mask) brighten

per_character_notes.Mochii: the garden's own pairing candidate lives here: Mochii's #50b0f0 against a pink taken from the scene's warm anchors — OUR pairing from OUR anchors, never a copied JoJo palette
per_character_notes.Sproutle: mint/leaf harmonise to the cool pole; the blue visor holds or deepens — it is already near the pairing's blue

recipes.decision_rule: Procedure steps 1-2 with signature_pair: choose a two-colour pairing FROM THE CAST'S AND PLACE'S OWN ANCHORS that gives the named feeling; assign poles per character by the feeling, not by base hue.
recipes.environment: takes the pairing fully — this is the recipe where the world is allowed to be prettiest
recipes.hold: the emotional peak's duration — a held pose, a shared beat, a resolution
kit_moves: feeling first (the recipe IS step 1, executed)
recipes.name: Emotion Bloom (Signature Pairing)
recipes.return: snap_back_on_ending_cut (or the grief-style within-scene restore when the bloom resolves into calm — named at board time)

default_transform.all_other_characters: hold base EXACTLY — any drift anywhere else dilutes the note
default_transform.the_noted_character_or_slot: one slot (or the whole palette of one character) transforms by the move the wrongness calls for — complement, inversion, or a hue the scene has not used

per_character_notes.Dorowani: a Dorowani note usually targets the accent: #a03436 is already licensed for wrongness, so a note ON Dorowani shifts the BODY and leaves the red — the red staying right is what makes the body read wrong
per_character_notes.Wispkin: the canonical house use: everything and everyone at base, the MASK alone shifted. The mask is a value accent — a shifted mask (a hue where white should be) is the garden's purest wrong note

recipes.decision_rule: Procedure steps 1-2 with wrong_note: restraint is the recipe. If two things feel wrong, the beat is a menace field, not a note.
recipes.environment: holds base exactly, unless the note IS the environment (one element of the place shifted — a single wrong-coloured tree, one leaf) — logged as the noted element
recipes.hold: until the wrongness is confronted, named, or exits — the note resolves by story, not by timer
recipes.name: The Wrong Note
recipes.return: snap_back_on_ending_cut — normally the cut where the wrongness is confronted or leaves

default_transform.accent: mute LAST — accents hold their hue longest and desaturate after everything else (identity lingers)
default_transform.support: desaturate + cool pull, ahead of dominant

per_character_notes.Kittember: the flame accent muting is the saddest legal image in this recipe — flame hue holds while its value falls
per_character_notes.Wispkin: already near-monochrome: grief takes Wispkin by VALUE (the whole figure dims) rather than saturation

recipes.decision_rule: Procedure steps 1-2 with mute_all: grief is the one feeling the kit answers by taking colour away. The order of muting (supports, dominants, accents last) is fixed by the recipe; the depth is the designer's call, logged.
recipes.environment: desaturates and cools with the characters — the world grieves at the same rate
recipes.hold: the grief beat's duration; grief beats run long by nature — the hold grammar allows it, the return is where discipline sits
recipes.name: Grief Mute
recipes.return: dissolve_exception: within-scene gradual restore as the feeling resolves (named at board time), or snap back if the scene cuts away unresolved

research_finding.honest_summary: There is no fixed formula and no lookup table in the documented method — inventing one would falsify the import. The method: a base palette exists so departures read; at a dramatic beat the colour decision is made per scene, FEELING FIRST, using a small kit of relationship moves (balance across opposing sides, symbolic fit, a trusted signature pairing, deliberate impossibility/inversion for world-rule breaks), applied with judgement by a named colour-design seat under the director's scene-specific policy. Shifts are total (characters included), sudden, held for the beat, and then the base palette returns. This library encodes THAT: procedure + kit + precedent recipes + logging.

status: draft v2 — the COLORWAY system: full palette shifts (environment AND characters), decided by the researched JoJo method (decision procedure, not a lookup table). Distinct from and coexisting with the CS lighting protocol (LIGHTING-SYSTEM §4), which governs light/tint only. Companion doc: COLORWAY-LIBRARY.md (§0 records the owner ruling this version implements; §1 records the research).
supersedes: v1 (2026-10-28, earlier draft) encoded lighting-grade shifts only, with character palettes locked under the CS protocol. That framing was withdrawn by the owner ruling of 2026-10-28: the lock governs environment tint, not colorways. v1's entries described CS-side lighting data and are superseded; the CS protocol itself is untouched and lives in LIGHTING-SYSTEM §4.

system_boundary.coexists_with: CS protocol (LIGHTING-SYSTEM §4) — LIGHTING shifts: keys, rims, atmosphere, shadow colour and grade of the LIGHT move; character fills are never re-hued by light (LS-2). That law stands, for lighting.
system_boundary.test: If a colour event can be removed by deleting an overlay, it was lighting. If it has to be repainted, it was a colorway.
system_boundary.this_system: COLORWAY shifts: the scene's palettes — environment AND characters — are re-decided for a dramatic beat, hold for the beat, and return to base. Palette replacement, not light behaviour.
system_boundary.wispkin_mask: The mask-white lock is an LS-2 TINT rule and binds lighting only. Under a colorway the mask is a palette slot like any other and CAN shift. Recipes that hold it white do so as a logged choice with a reason.

transform_kit._note: Relationship moves, not palettes. Each is grounded in the research (§1 of the companion doc): balance and symbolic fit and the signature pairing are Araki's own stated practice; inversion is the documented world-break grammar; unification/opposition/surge/mute are the observed anime shift shapes, labelled secondary in the doc.
transform_kit.invert_world: global inversion: hues to complements, values inverted — reserved for world-rule breaks (CW-B5)
transform_kit.mute_all: global desaturation + cooling, accents muting last
transform_kit.oppose_poles: the frame's two sides take complementary poles; characters move by allegiance
transform_kit.signature_pair: field and characters re-paired around a trusted two-colour pairing chosen from the cast's own anchors
transform_kit.surge_self: one character surges (saturation/value up, dominant toward its accent family); all others step back one step
transform_kit.unify_to_field: all palettes (environment + characters) pulled toward one field hue family; accents hold longest
transform_kit.wrong_note: exactly one element shifts; everything else holds base exactly
